newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up slightly, wary of stocks.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up slightly, wary of stocks.

text.p: *Australian bond yields rose slightly in early trading with one wary eye on global stocks after the hefty plunge in the U.S. equity market on Friday.
Australian bond yields rose slightly in early trading with one wary eye on global stocks after the hefty plunge in the U.S. equity market on Friday.
The Dow Jones industrial average shed 247 points, its second largest one day point loss ever amid concerns over future company profits and a sharp drop in the U.S. dollar.
"The stock market is the only factor this morning, but I'm a bit surprised by our weakness, and I thought we might have been a buy if stocks are under pressure," one trader said.
Indeed, the short end of the U.S. Treasury had benefitted from a flight-to-quality on Friday as stocks fell.

Fears of tighter German monetary policy depressed the U.S. currency, although this week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting is not expected to lift interest rates in the wake of a run favourable inflation data.

Local data is again fairly thin this week with company profits due on Thursday and the latest report on enterprise bargaining agreements from the Department of Industrial Relations is expected at some stage during the week.
However, with average weekly earning data remaining benign in the second quarter, the latter is not likely to stir much reaction in the market, analysts said.

Yield differentials to the dollar bloc were mixed with the local market giving up some ground to the U.S. after the strong outperformance late last week. This contraction had followed a more subdued than expected outcome to the final quarter wages report, which has prompted thoughts of a further policy easing.
